# Build-backend constraint for RELEASE builds only (issue #163).
#
# `tooling/sanitizer/pyproject.toml` declares `build-system.requires =
# ["hatchling>=1.27"]` -- a floor, not a pin, so an ordinary
# `python -m build` resolves whatever hatchling exists at that moment.
# That is the right default for a tool people are meant to fork and
# rebuild: constraining the backend in `pyproject.toml` would push the
# pin onto downstream packagers building from the sdist.
#
# It is the wrong default for the bytes we publish. This package's whole
# pitch is "this artifact came from this workflow," and a release built
# by an unnamed backend version weakens that claim: two tags cut a month
# apart could produce different metadata for identical source, and the
# PEP 740 attestation would faithfully attest to both.
#
# So the pin lives here, applied via `PIP_CONSTRAINT` on the release
# build step only. Bumping it is a visible, reviewable one-line diff on
# a PR rather than a silent resolution at tag time.
#
# This is not theoretical. Verified locally 2026-08-18 by building this
# package twice against the same source: hatchling 1.27.0 produces
# `Metadata-Version: 2.4`, hatchling 1.32.0 produces `2.5` (PEP 794). The
# backend version therefore decides a metadata field that the index itself
# can accept or reject -- Warehouse refused 2.5 uploads outright until
# 2026-02-17. An unpinned release build lets that field change without a
# diff, and `twine check --strict` will not notice, because it validates the
# metadata it understands rather than asking the server.
#
# Chosen 2026-08-18: latest hatchling at the time #163 landed.
hatchling==1.32.0
